brief: I'm Marcy Voss, the secretary at Grace Lutheran Church in Findlay, Ohio. I need a flyer for our Fall Festival, as a 1080 x 1350 portrait image we can post on Facebook and print at 8 x 10. Facts: Saturday, October 18, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., on the church lawn and in the fellowship hall at 412 Maple Street. Free admission. Pie contest at noon (bring your pie by 11:30), a cake walk, hayrides for the kids, a chili cook-off judged at 1:30, and a bake sale to benefit the youth mission trip. Rain moves everything into the fellowship hall. Our colors are a deep green and a warm gold, but we are not tied to them. No logo to use. Do not invent anything not listed here (no phone number, no website, no sponsors). Don't ask me questions.

I'm Caleb Tarrant. My family's bluegrass band, The Tarrant Brothers and Daughter (me, my brother Wes, and my daughter Annie on fiddle), is putting out our first album. It's called 'Sorghum Hill' and it's 11 songs recorded live in a barn in Pike County, Kentucky in one weekend. I need the cover as a 1400 x 1400 square. Text on the cover: the band name and the album title. Nothing else is needed, but a small line 'Recorded live in a barn' is fine if it earns its place. No photos available, so it has to be type, shape and color only (inline SVG is fine). The sound is old-time and warm, not slick. Do not invent song titles or credits. Don't ask me questions.

I run Hartwell Hardware in Bellefontaine, Ohio. My grandfather opened it in 1955, so this year is our 70th anniversary. I need a 1080 x 1080 square graphic for Facebook and Instagram. Facts: the sale is Friday through Sunday, November 14 to 16; 20% off any single regular-priced item all three days; free coffee and donuts Saturday morning from 8 to 10; and the first 70 customers on Saturday get a hardware-store yardstick with our name on it. We're at 118 East Columbus Avenue. Store hours that weekend are the usual 7:30 to 6 on Friday, 7:30 to 5 on Saturday, 10 to 3 on Sunday. We are not a slick brand; we're a hardware store. Do not invent a logo, a phone number or any other offer. Don't ask me questions.

I own Brightline Mobile Detailing in Columbia, South Carolina. It's me, Tre Washington, and one part-time helper; we drive to the customer's driveway. I want a 30-second vertical (9:16) video for Instagram Reels and TikTok that gets people to book a spot. Facts: full interior and exterior detail, $180 for a sedan and $220 for an SUV; we use a steam cleaner and a foam cannon; we do about three cars a day, booking is by text or on the website; our van is matte gray with a thin orange stripe. I have no footage, so every shot will be generated by a video model. Make the whole production plan. Don't ask me questions.

I'm the communications volunteer at Trinity Presbyterian in Dayton, Ohio. I need a 35-second widescreen (16:9) invitation video for our Christmas Eve candlelight service, to play before services and post online. Facts: two services on December 24, at 4 p.m. (family service with children's choir) and 9 p.m. (candlelight with communion); childcare for under 4 at the 4 o'clock; the sanctuary is old brick with tall clear windows; we sing 'Silent Night' with candles at the end of each service; parking is behind the church off Wilkinson Street. We want it to feel quiet and warm, not like a commercial. All shots will be generated by a video model, and we want no recognizable faces of real people. Make the whole production plan. Don't ask me questions.

I'm Ingrid Solberg. I make cutting boards and small tables in a one-person shop in Duluth, Minnesota under the name Solberg Woodworks. I want a 25-second widescreen (16:9) craft film for my website's home page, looping silently is fine but I would like a sound plan too. Facts: I work in hard maple, walnut and cherry; every board is hand-planed and finished with a mineral oil and beeswax blend I mix myself; the shop is an old garage with one big north window; a board takes about six hours start to finish; I sell at the Duluth farmers market and online. No people's faces should appear (hands are fine). All shots will be generated by a video model. Make the whole production plan. Don't ask me questions.

I host a small-town history podcast. The file voice_raw.wav is my recording of one segment (mono, 44.1 kHz, about 45 seconds, 16-bit). It was recorded in a spare bedroom next to a refrigerator: there is a low electrical hum, hiss, I drift away from the mic in two places so those parts are quiet, I popped a P and clipped it once, and the room is echoey. Clean it up so it is ready to publish: remove the hum and hiss without making me sound underwater, bring the quiet parts up to match, tame the pop, and deliver at -16 LUFS integrated with a true peak no higher than -1 dBTP. Keep the same length and keep it sounding like a real person in a real room, not a robot. Don't ask me questions.

I run the sound for our church's weekly video. voice.wav is the pastor reading the announcements (mono, 44.1 kHz, about 28 seconds, already clean). music.wav is a soft instrumental bed (stereo, 44.1 kHz, 60 seconds) and it is mixed much louder than the voice. Build the finished announcement: music fades in over 3 seconds, the pastor starts 4 seconds in, the music drops well below the voice while he speaks and comes back up in the pauses between sentences, and after he finishes the music rises for a moment and fades out over 4 seconds. The finished file should end about 4 seconds after the last word. Deliver stereo at -16 LUFS integrated with a true peak no higher than -1 dBTP. The words must stay easy to understand. Don't ask me questions.

I'm the owner of Findlay Feed & Seed and I'm buying a 15-second spot on the local AM station. I recorded three lines separately: line1.wav, line2.wav and line3.wav (mono, 44.1 kHz, clean; each a few seconds). music.wav is a 30-second bed (stereo) and sting.wav is a 1.5-second closing chime. Assemble the spot, exactly 15 seconds long (give or take a quarter second): music starts on the first frame, line 1 comes in at about 0.5 seconds, then line 2, then line 3, in that order, each separated by a short breath of about half a second, with the music ducked under the voice and coming up between lines; the sting plays at the end, and everything ends cleanly by 15.0 seconds with no click or abrupt cut. Radio is loud: deliver stereo at -16 LUFS integrated, true peak no higher than -1 dBTP. Don't ask me questions.

Write the email to our congregation. I'm Pastor Dale Hutchins at Cornerstone Baptist in Lima, Ohio. Facts: our boiler failed on Tuesday and the fix is $14,200; the insurance won't cover it because the boiler is 31 years old; we have $5,300 in the building fund; the deacons voted to ask the church for the remaining $8,900 over the next four Sundays; Sunday services continue as normal in the sanctuary, which is heated by the separate gas unit, but the fellowship hall and the nursery are closed until the new boiler is in, expected November 21; Wednesday night supper moves to the sanctuary. I don't want to guilt anyone and I don't want anyone giving beyond what they can. Gifts can go in the offering plate marked 'boiler' or be given online on the church website. Write it now, don't ask me questions.

Write a blog post for my website explaining a price change. I'm Mara Okafor and I run Muddy Paws Mobile Grooming in Tulsa, Oklahoma, out of a converted van. Facts: starting January 1 a full groom for a small dog goes from $85 to $95, and a large dog from $120 to $135; my cost for shampoo, blades, water heater propane and the van's insurance went up about 18% since 2023 and I haven't raised prices since March 2023; I keep three Saturday slots a month at $60 for seniors and for rescue dogs; I've groomed about 1,900 dogs since I started in 2021; my oldest regular is a 16-year-old beagle named Biscuit; existing clients can keep the old price on any appointment booked before December 15. I want people to understand and not feel nickel-and-dimed. Write it now, don't ask me questions.

Write the event page for our fundraiser run. I'm Lt. Ray Pruitt of the Harmon Township Volunteer Fire Department in Wayne County, Ohio. Facts: the Harvest Dash 5K and 1-mile fun walk is Saturday, October 4; check-in is 7:30 a.m. at the firehouse on County Road 21; the 5K starts at 8:30 and the fun walk at 8:45; entry is $25 for the 5K and $10 for the walk, kids under 8 free; the first 150 registered get a shirt; the course is mostly flat gravel and road through the Hostetler farm lane, not stroller friendly past the first mile; pancakes are served after at the firehouse for $5 a plate; the money goes toward a new set of rescue tools, which cost about $38,000; we raised $6,100 last year with 112 runners. Register at harmondash.example or on race day. Write it now, don't ask me questions.

I run Hollis Creek Canoe Rental in Hollis, New Hampshire. I shot four clips on different cameras and I need them cut together into one video for my website. The clips are in this folder: clip_a.mp4 (1280x720, 30 fps, 12 s), clip_b.mp4 (1920x1080, 24 fps, 10 s), clip_c.mp4 (a vertical phone clip, 720x1280, 30 fps, 8 s) and clip_d.mp4 (1280x720, 25 fps, 9 s); music.wav (45 s) is the music bed. Write a bash script that uses only ffmpeg and cuts them into one finished video called out.mp4, 1280x720, 30 fps, H.264 video with AAC audio, between 22 and 28 seconds long, with at least five cuts or transitions between shots, using material from all four clips (the vertical clip must not be stretched). Put the title 'Hollis Creek Canoe Rental' on screen near the start, and a closing card with the text 'Open May to October - Rt 122, Hollis NH' at the end. The music runs under the whole piece, fading in at the start and out at the end, at about -16 LUFS integrated. Avoid any black frames longer than half a second. Don't ask me questions.
